blocks.value: **Polymorphism is the ability of an object to take on many forms.**

items: **The most common use of polymorphism occurs when a base class reference is used to refer to a derived class object.**
**When an overridden method is invoked, its action is the one defined in the class used to create the object with `new`. It is not determined by the type of the variable naming the object.**

**Dynamic binding** allows many meanings to be associated with one method name. In dynamic binding, the definition of a method is not bound to an invocation until **run time**, when the method is called. This is the mechanism used by polymorphism.

**Even though `p` is of type `Person`, the `writeOutput()` method associated with `Undergraduate` or `Student` is invoked, depending on which class was used to create the object.**

Look at what that buys you. The loop says `p.writeOutput()` **once**. It produces three different outputs, chosen per object at run time. Add a `GraduateStudent` class tomorrow, drop it into the array, and **this loop needs no changes at all**: it already handles a class that did not exist when it was written.
Without polymorphism, the loop would need a chain of `if` tests naming every subclass, and every new subclass would mean editing every such chain in the program.
